LanguageData.RealRuins_ModOptions_AllowUploads: Allow uploading your bases to ruins database
LanguageData.RealRuins_ModOptions_AllowDownloadsToolt: If you switch this off, it won't remove anything you have already downloaded.
LanguageData.RealRuins_ModOptions_AllowUploadsTooltip: It's recommended to keep this on to help populate the database with various interesting base designs. This should not consume more than several megabytes per game session.
LanguageData.RealRuins_ModOptions_CacheSizeTooltip: Even if you reach this limit, the mod will continue downloading new blueprints, removing the older ones.
LanguageData.RealRuins_ModOptions_OfflineModeTooltip: This mode will delete all cached data that was downloaded from the server and prevent any further uploads and downloads. However, your own bases will still be stored locally and used for creating ruins in your game.
LanguageData.RealRuins_MapOptions_DensityTT: Average number of ruins spawned on 100x100 area
LanguageData.RealRuins_MapOptions_SizeTT: Ruins area is selected randomly in the range from 50% to 150% of the entered value
LanguageData.RealRuins_MapOptions_DeteriorationTT: This value determines additional chance for a tile to be destroyed and does not influence the remaining hit points. Zero is the default setting, max will result in no ruins at all.
LanguageData.RealRuins_MapOptions_WealthPerMapTT: Total market value that all scattered ruins of one map may have together (things and floors). Most maps stay well below the default; on a map with an unusually rich ruin its most valuable things are taken away until the ruins fit. Rightmost position: no limit. Does not affect pristine ruins, planetary locations and the main ruin of a caravan event.
LanguageData.RealRuins_MapOptions_WealthScaleWithProx: Raise the limit near settlements and lower it far from them, the same way the number of ruins changes with proximity, so each ruin keeps about the same share. Off: ruins near settlements share one limit, so the dense ruins there are more picked over. Needs proximity to be enabled.
LanguageData.RealRuins_MapOptions_WealthIgnoreStructu: Plain walls, doors and floors (up to 50 silver per tile) don't count toward the limit and are never removed for it: there are lots of them and they are not loot. Golden walls, silver floors, autodoors and the like still count.
LanguageData.RealRuins_MapOptions_WealthCountDamage: Count damaged things at lower value
LanguageData.RealRuins_MapOptions_WealthCountDamageTT: Off: everything counts at full price, since repairing restores it and a damaged thing often works just as well. On: the actual market value of what spawned is counted (damage lowers it, quality changes it), so more fits into the limit.
LanguageData.RealRuins_MapOptions_CostLimitTT: Things worth more than this are removed from regular ruins. Caravan ruins and planetary locations have their own fixed limits. Rightmost position: no limit.
LanguageData.RealRuins_MapOptions_DisableHaulablesTT: No haulable items will spawn, but furniture may still appear. Applies to regular ruins, caravan ruins and ruined planetary locations, not to pristine ruins and intact locations.
LanguageData.RealRuins_MapOptions_WallsAndDoorsOnlyTT: This setting is pretty aggressive and will remove everything that is not based on a vanilla wall or a door. Applies to regular ruins, caravan ruins and ruined planetary locations, not to pristine ruins and intact locations.
LanguageData.RealRuins_MapOptions_DisableHostilesTT: Chance for every ruin fragment that animals (80%) or mechanoids (20%) live in it. Other ruins have fixed values: caravan ruins 80%, pristine ruins always, planetary locations never. Threat scale still applies to all of them.
LanguageData.RealRuins_MapOptions_EnableProximityTT: Settlement proximity influences generation parameters: ruins are denser near cities, but also emptier.
LanguageData.RealRuins_MapOptions_StartWithoutRuinsTT: No ruins will be generated on the starting map. Later ruins will be generated normally according to settings.
LanguageData.RealRuins.CacheSettings.Caption: Cache and storage
LanguageData.RealRuins.CacheSettings.Description: Where blueprints come from and where they are stored on your disk.
LanguageData.RealRuins_ModOptions_ClearCacheConfirm: Are you sure you want to clear all cached snapshots, including planetary ruins blueprints? This action cannot be undone.
LanguageData.RealRuins_ModOptions_OfflineModeConfirm:
Local mode deletes all ruins blueprints downloaded from the server as soon as you close the settings. Only your own bases and the blueprints of planetary ruins are kept.

If you change your mind later, you will have to switch local mode off and download the blueprints again, which can take several minutes. Until then, ruins are built from your own bases only.

Switch to local mode?
LanguageData.RealRuins.CacheSettings.PlanetaryDescrip: Blueprints downloaded for planetary ruins are stored separately for every world seed, coverage and map size.
LanguageData.RealRuins.CacheSettings.PlanetaryEmpty: No planetary ruins blueprints are stored.
LanguageData.RealRuins.CacheSettings.ClearFolderConfi: Remove all {1} planetary ruins blueprints ({2}) stored for seed "{0}"? Worlds with this seed will download them again when needed.
LanguageData.RealRuins_ModOptions_DownloadMoreTooltip: Download additional blueprints from the server.
LanguageData.RealRuins.SpawnSettings.Caption: Spawn and tech level
LanguageData.RealRuins.SpawnSettings.Description: What the ruins look like: how many, how big, how worn, and what may appear in them. The wealth limits are on the Wealth and balance tab.
LanguageData.RealRuins.KeepVanillaRuinsTT: If enabled, vanilla RimWorld ruins will be preserved alongside Real Ruins.
LanguageData.RealRuins.PlanetarySettings.Caption: Planetary ruins and locations
LanguageData.RealRuins.PlanetarySettings.Enable: Offer to load planetary locations at game start
LanguageData.RealRuins.PlanetarySettings.DownloadLimi: Maximum number of blueprints to download
LanguageData.RealRuins.PlanetarySettings.TransferLimi: Maximum number of locations to spawn
LanguageData.RealRuins.PlanetarySettings.DisableFrien: If enabled, world locations will be occupied by hostile factions only.
LanguageData.RealRuins.PlanetarySettings.RemoveAllCon: Are you sure you want to remove all locations spawned by Real Ruins?
LanguageData.RealRuins.PlanetaryLoader.DisableFriendl: If enabled, world locations will be occupied by hostile factions only.
LanguageData.LetterCaravanEnteredRuins: {0} has arrived at the abandoned base ruins and is ready to begin scavenging.
LanguageData.RealRuins.CaravanFoundRuins: During their travel, {0} spotted a bunch of destroyed buildings nearby, which seem to be in better condition than usual. There are probably still some valuables left. On the other hand, there might be a wild animal lair, a mechanoid nest or a raider outpost: there must be a reason why those buildings seem untouched.
LanguageData.RealRuins.SmallRuinsInspectString: Small abandoned buildings. Something valuable may still be inside.
LanguageData.DeterioratedArtDescription: This item is too worn and damaged. You can tell for sure it was a beautiful art object once, but now you can hardly guess what it was about.
LanguageData.RealRuins.NoMoreEnemies: Looks like no one's gonna show up anymore. You can safely pack up and leave.
LanguageData.RealRuins.PristineRuinsIncidentRetired.T: The "nearby ruins found" incident was removed, nothing has been spawned. Pristine ruins now come as a quest. To create one manually, use Debug actions -> Generate quest -> RealRuins_AbandonedBase.
LanguageData.RealRuins.ReformLockedManual: Raiders may still show up. Pick up what your pawns can carry and leave via the map edge, or wait until things calm down.
LanguageData.RealRuins.DescPOI0: A small group of buildings, presumably military. Probably an armoury or a small transit military base. It can have several stationary weapons and a dozen or two soldiers.
LanguageData.RealRuins.DescPOI1: A very small military outpost: a couple of rooms, a couple of turrets, a couple of soldiers.
LanguageData.RealRuins.DescPOI2: A temporary camp set up for mining or hunting, or as a transshipment point.
LanguageData.RealRuins.DescPOI3: A large thriving city. Even though it usually does not have massive walls or a lot of stationary weapons, it can request powerful reinforcements in case of an assault.
LanguageData.RealRuins.DescPOI4: Those buildings contain a lot of workbenches and produced goods. Most likely the factory is well guarded.
LanguageData.RealRuins.DescPOI5: This research and development center is focused on production, but its goods are more sophisticated and pricey than in a regular factory. Most likely it's well guarded and guards will call reinforcements as soon as you decide to assault.
LanguageData.RealRuins.DescPOI6: A group of buildings focused primarily on power production.
LanguageData.RealRuins.DescPOI7: A large military base with lots of stationary weapons, several dozens of personnel and reinforcements ready to arrive.
LanguageData.RealRuins.DescPOI8: From a distance it looks like a large hangar filled with goods. And a lot of guards.
LanguageData.RealRuins.DescPOI9: A small building that looks like a communication center. Probably just a temporary military camp with only a few guards.
LanguageData.RealRuins.DescPOI10: Remains of some buildings, bits of furniture, broken workbenches, pipes and metal bars. You can't tell what it was long ago: all that's left are empty ruins.
LanguageData.RealRuins.DescPOI11: Heavily guarded stronghold. Extremely well defended with tons of stationary weapons, troops and reinforcements.
LanguageData.RealRuins.DescPOI12: A village of farmers and craftsmen. Its houses are simple, but the villagers will defend them.
LanguageData.RealRuins.DescPOI13: A castle behind thick walls. A garrison of armed men guards it, and its lord will not give it up without a fight.
LanguageData.RealRuins.DescPOI14: Workshops full of benches, tools and finished goods made by hand. The craftsmen keep a few guards to protect their wares.
LanguageData.RealRuins.DescPOI15: A gravship that landed here and never took off again. Its hull still holds whatever the crew carried, and someone may have moved in.
LanguageData.RealRuins.POINowRuined: This {0} was once full of life, but now it's abandoned, and no one knows why. So better beware of all kinds of danger.
LanguageData.RealRuins.POIUselessRuins: You wonder what it could have been long ago. Now it's mostly rock and rubble.
LanguageData.LetterCaravanEnteredUnownedPOI: {0} has arrived at the destination. Proceed with caution.
LanguageData.LetterTransportPodsArrivedInUnownedPOI: Transport pods have arrived at the destination.
LanguageData.LetterTransportPodsAttackedPOI: Transport pods have arrived at the destination. The attack has begun.
LanguageData.LetterLabelTransportPodsArrivedAtRuins: Transport pods have arrived at the ruins
LanguageData.LetterTransportPodsArrivedAtRuins: Transport pods have arrived at the ruins.
LanguageData.RealRuins.PlanetaryLoader.LoadBlueprints: This feature will load maps of other players who had their colonies on the same planet. Their colonies will be spawned as other factions' settlements and outposts, or as abandoned ruins. Unlike random ruins, those will be placed at their original locations.
LanguageData.RealRuins.PlanetaryLoader.OptionsDescrip: In this mode you can control every step. First you load only the number of blueprints available for the planet and choose how many of them you want to download. Then, after loading, you choose how many of them you want to transfer and how they should be filtered. You can stop at any step, remove everything and start over.
LanguageData.RealRuins.PlanetaryLoader.MapSizeChangeW: WARNING: If you're going to change map size, press Close now and download blueprints after changing map size.
LanguageData.RealRuins.PlanetaryLoader.LowCountWarnin: You have too few blueprints. If it bothers you, try selecting another seed or other map settings. You can check the most populated worlds by visiting https://woolstrand.art/view/maps/topseeds
LanguageData.RealRuins.PlanetaryLoader.NoBlueprintsWa: This world does not contain any maps. It means nobody has played with the same seed, coverage and map size yet. If you want to have some locations on the world map, try selecting a more common seed. You can check the most populated worlds by visiting https://woolstrand.art/view/maps/topseeds
LanguageData.RealRuins.PlanetaryLoader.LoadedAmount: Server has {0} blueprints for this planet.
LanguageData.RealRuins.PlanetaryLoader.TooManyBluepri: Seems there are a whole lot of blueprints!

The server says this world has {0} blueprints. This can take a while to download and process, and the world map can become cluttered. If it's your first time using this game mode, it's recommended to limit blueprint count.
Show advanced settings and let me decide
LanguageData.RealRuins.PlanetaryLoader.BiomeFiltering: Exclude maps with missing or mismatching biome
LanguageData.RealRuins.PlanetaryLoader.CostFilteringT: Exclude maps with too low cost (lower than average "empty" map)
LanguageData.RealRuins.PlanetaryLoader.AreaFilteringT: Exclude maps with too small area and too low items count
LanguageData.RealRuins.PlanetaryLoader.DiscardAbandon: Discard all maps that do not qualify as any specific kind of POI (this usually drops about a half of all maps)
LanguageData.RealRuins.PlanetaryLoader.NeedsGameInPro: You have to be in an ongoing game to use this menu
LanguageData.RealRuins.CaravanReformTooltip:
How you leave pristine ruins.

Automatic: works the same way as forming a caravan on your home map.

Instant: a button on the world map reforms the caravan at once, when no enemies are around.

Manual: no reforming until the raids are over. Pick up the items by hand and leave via the map edge.
LanguageData.RealRuins.ForceMultiplierTT: Scales every threat Real Ruins creates: the animals and mechanoids in regular ruins, the raiders at caravan ruins, the raids and raid triggers at pristine ruins, and the starting parties. 0 means no inhabitants, raiders or raid triggers at all.
LanguageData.RealRuins.AbsoluteWealthCapTT: The most pristine ruins (the quest) may be worth. Caravan ruins have their own limit. Wooden walls and doors are not counted.
LanguageData.RealRuins.UseForcesGenerationV2TT: While you're at pristine ruins, small groups of enemies keep arriving, a few at a time, on top of the big raids. The more loot is still left, the more of them come. As you carry it off, they thin out. Turn this off to get only the big raids.
LanguageData.RealRuins.DisableFriendlyRaidsTT: If enabled, only hostile factions will spawn raids during ruins events. Friendly faction raids will be prevented.
LanguageData.RealRuins.SpawnRoofsTT: If disabled, ruins of all kinds (including points of interest and abandoned bases) are generated without roofs. Roofs that collapsed from deterioration stay collapsed either way.
LanguageData.RealRuins.SpawnBlacklistTT: Comma-separated list of item defs to exclude from spawning.
LanguageData.RealRuins.MaterialBlacklistTT: Comma-separated list of materials to exclude from spawning. When a thing made of a blacklisted material is encountered, it will be replaced with the fallback material.
LanguageData.RealRuins.FallbackMaterialTT: Material to use when a blacklisted material is encountered. Default is Wood. If invalid or empty, items with blacklisted materials will be discarded.
LanguageData.RealRuins.TechLimit.Caption: Tech Level
LanguageData.RealRuins.TechLimit.EnabledTT: Things more advanced than the selected tech level are removed from ruins. A thing's tech level comes from its own tech level, the research needed to build or craft it and its ingredients. Walls and doors above the limit are replaced with plain stone walls and wooden doors. Things with no tech level at all always stay.
LanguageData.RealRuins.TechLimit.MaxLevelTT: The most advanced tech level of things which can spawn in ruins.
LanguageData.RealRuins.TechLimit.StrategyTT: Strict: nothing above the limit ever spawns. Good for true medieval or fantasy playthroughs.\n\nLimited: things above the limit are rare relics of the past: 10% of them stay one level above the limit, 1% two levels above, and so on. Good for post-apocalyptic low tech playthroughs.
LanguageData.RealRuins.TechLimit.RuinsTT: Ruins scattered over newly generated maps.
LanguageData.RealRuins.TechLimit.POIsTT: Locations created from other players' bases when a new game starts, ruined or inhabited. The location type is decided after the limit is applied, and inhabitants come from factions of the allowed tech level. Type and inhabitants are picked when a location is created, so for existing locations only their contents change.
LanguageData.RealRuins.TechLimit.EventsTT: Pristine ruins and small ruins spotted by caravans.
LanguageData.RealRuins.FactionOwnedStartTileDesc: You're about to enter a tile with a settlement on it, and this settlement belongs to another faction. You can either make it abandoned and settle in the ruins, make it yours, or you can attack it with your starting party.
LanguageData.RealRuins.DebugSettings.Caption: Debug Settings
LanguageData.RealRuins.DebugSettings.ResetSettingsCon: Are you sure you want to reset all settings to their default values?
LanguageData.RealRuins.DebugSettings.KeepSnapshotsAft: When enabled, snapshot files will be kept in the temp directory after uploading instead of being deleted. Useful for debugging upload issues.
LanguageData.RealRuins.DebugSettings.LogRuinsWealthTo: When enabled, every generated ruin logs its estimated wealth (new and legacy cost schemes) and the actual market value of what was spawned, and every map with scattered ruins logs a summary. Logged regardless of the log level. Also toggled from the dev mode debug actions menu (RealRuins).
LanguageData.RealRuins.DebugSettings.UseStagingEnviro: When enabled, all API requests go to staging.woolstrand.art and blueprints are stored in the staging bucket (realruins-staging, sfo3). Disable for normal play.
LanguageData.RealRuins.DebugSettings.ManualUploadTool: Manually trigger a blueprint capture and upload of the current map. Useful for testing upload functionality.
LanguageData.RealRuins.DebugSettings.UploadTriggered: Blueprint capture triggered. Check logs for details.
LanguageData.RealRuins.DebugSettings.NoMap: No map available. Please load a game first.
LanguageData.RealRuins.EnableAbandonedRuinsFoundEvent: When enabled, you can get a quest to large pristine ruins nearby: rich and untouched, but contested by raiders.
LanguageData.RealRuins.EnableCaravanFoundRuinsEventTT: When enabled, travelling caravans can spot a small ruin nearby and give you the option to investigate it.
LanguageData.RealRuins.ScaleWithColonyWealth: Scale all limits with colony wealth
LanguageData.RealRuins.ScaleWithColonyWealthTT: All ruins wealth limits are multiplied by your colony wealth divided by the value below: a richer colony finds richer ruins, a poorer one poorer ruins, but at least half of each limit. Limits can go above what you set this way. Unlimited ruins stay unlimited. Colony wealth is counted the way the storyteller does, over your home maps and caravans.
LanguageData.RealRuins.ReferenceColonyWealth: Colony wealth the limits are set for
LanguageData.RealRuins.ReferenceColonyWealthTT: At this colony wealth all ruins wealth limits are exactly what you set. At twice this wealth they are doubled.
LanguageData.RealRuins.POIRuinsCostCapTT: The most an abandoned location on the planet may be worth. Most of them are worth less than this.
LanguageData.RealRuins.CaravanRuinsCostCapTT: The most a ruin spotted by a caravan may be worth. Its most valuable things are taken away until it fits. Raiders at the ruin scale with what is left.
LanguageData.RealRuins.Settings.ImportFailed: Failed to import settings. The string may be invalid or corrupted.
LanguageData.RealRuins.Presets.Caption: Presets
LanguageData.RealRuins.Presets.Description: Quick setups for common ways to play. A preset changes only the settings it is about: your cache, network and debug settings and your item blacklist are never touched. Play style and tech level presets don't affect each other.
LanguageData.RealRuins.Presets.DefaultTT: Ruins the way the mod comes out of the box. Resets wealth, threats, spawn and event settings, but not the tech level.
LanguageData.RealRuins.Presets.TechNormalTT: No tech level limit: anything the original base had may spawn.
LanguageData.RealRuins.Presets.TechNeolithicTT: Nothing above the neolithic level ever spawns, in any ruins or locations.
LanguageData.RealRuins.Presets.TechMedievalTT: A medieval or fantasy world: nothing above the medieval level ever spawns, in any ruins or locations.
LanguageData.RealRuins.Presets.TechPostApocalypticTT: A medieval world after a cataclysm: most things are medieval or older, but rare relics of the industrial and spacer past still turn up.
LanguageData.RealRuins.Presets.ResetAllTT: Resets every Real Ruins setting to its default, including cache, network and debug settings. The Default play style preset resets only the play style settings.
LanguageData.RealRuins.WealthSettings.Caption: Wealth and balance
LanguageData.RealRuins.WealthSettings.Description: How much the ruins on your map may be worth, and how dangerous they are. The limits are the main balance tool: whatever else you set, ruins never exceed them.
LanguageData.RealRuins.Settings.RegularLimitCounting: Regular ruins: how the limit counts
LanguageData.RealRuins.TechLimit.AppliesHereTT: Part of the tech level limit at the top of this page: it only works while the limit is on.
LanguageData.RealRuins.GameplaySettings.Caption: Gameplay
LanguageData.RealRuins.GameplaySettings.Description: Which special sites exist in your game and how you interact with them.
LanguageData.RealRuins.CacheSettings.StagingWarning: Staging server is on (Debug tab). Turn it off for normal play.
LanguageData.RealRuins.DebugSettings.Description: Logging and developer tools. You only need these when you report a bug.
